headline: High-risk shared-workspace interaction: Roo Code can write/modify workspace state while RD-Agent can exfiltrate via broad network egress, creating leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP; RD-Agent can emit logs/files and run browsers. A shared workspace or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content from RD-Agent influence Roo Code, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, prompt-like content can cross from RD-Agent to Roo Code.
IF Roo Code consumes RD-Agent-generated files or MCP messages as instructions, injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories per agent.
Disable MCP for the pair unless explicitly needed.
Treat RD-Agent outputs as untrusted text in Roo Code prompts.
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on any RD-Agent-produced file.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs, and has broad network egress. Roo Code reads workspace files and can send them to configured model APIs or MCP servers. If they share files, sensitive data can flow from RD-Agent into Roo Code and then out over network egress, so the default blast radius is exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace, RD-Agent data can become visible to Roo Code.
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API or MCP server, workspace contents can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate, access-controlled workspaces.
Remove sensitive datasets from any shared directory.
Disable network egress for one agent during joint runs.
Restrict Roo Code to local-only models for shared tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or redaction on workspace reads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs/files. In a shared workspace, both can mutate the same repo or files without documented locking, making conflicting writes and git corruption plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same VS Code workspace or git repository, concurrent writes can collide.
IF RD-Agent and Roo Code both edit the same files without external locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or repo clone.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use file locks or a single-writer policy.
Review git diffs before commit actions.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and execute shell commands; RD-Agent produces logs, traces, and research outputs that Roo Code may treat as authoritative. Without a verification gate, RD-Agent mistakes can cascade into Roo Code edits, commits, or commands, and the downstream blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses RD-Agent outputs as inputs for code changes or shell actions, errors can propagate.
IF Roo Code commits or executes commands based on unverified RD-Agent artifacts, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review of RD-Agent outputs before Roo Code acts.
Use a checklist for any shell or git action.
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for research artifacts.
Keep RD-Agent outputs in a quarantine folder.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff files.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports and competition datasets, while Roo Code can read workspace files and send them to configured APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create a retention or residency mismatch, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction or certification conflict, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, Roo Code may transmit it to external model APIs.
IF the operator relies on differing retention policies between the agents, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Use approved local or enterprise model endpoints only.
Document retention and deletion handling for both agents.
Restrict access to competition or financial datasets.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
